quickAnswer: Oil heats 64.2% of Boylston's occupied homes, 6th-highest of the 50 towns, while utility gas reaches only 16.9% (ACS 2022). The town also runs its own Municipal Light Department, which shapes the heat pump rebate path.
body: ## Oil first, gas a distant second

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) finds 1,196 of Boylston's 1,864 occupied homes burning fuel oil or kerosene. That share, 64.2%, ranks 6th of the 50 towns Mass HVAC serves, against 36.5% for the middle town. Utility gas heats 315 homes (16.9%), which ranks 45th. Electricity heats 203 (10.9%), 22nd, and bottled or tank gas heats 102 (5.5%), 17th.

Behind those figures is a plain decision for many owners. When an oil boiler or furnace wears out, the choice is a new oil unit, gas if a main is close enough to extend, or a heat pump. Gas is available to relatively few homes today, so the oil-versus-heat-pump comparison comes up first.
## A municipal light department

The sheet confirms that Boylston's electric utility is the Boylston Municipal Light Department, a municipal utility. That matters for rebates, because a municipal utility narrows the Mass Save route and brings in the utility's own program. Oil is far ahead of gas here, so homes on oil would generally begin with the light department's program. The [heat pump page](/cities/boylston/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers the details, and the department itself can say what its program offers.
## A small town with a large reservoir

Boylston has 4,855 residents, the 48th-largest population of the 50 towns, and 1,896 housing units. Its area is 19.7 square miles, of which 16.0 are land and 3.6 are water (18.50%). The Wachusett Reservoir, part of the water supply system managed by the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority for the Greater Boston area, lies in the northwestern part of the town and covers about 5,000 acres.

The town maintains about 45 miles of roadway and 9 miles of sidewalks. It has its own Municipal Light Department and Water District, and a volunteer fire and ambulance service. Its neighbors are Shrewsbury, West Boylston, Sterling, Clinton, Berlin and Northborough. Boylston and Berlin share the Berlin-Boylston Regional School District, with Tahanto Regional Middle/High School serving both, and the Worcester County Horticultural Society runs Tower Hill Botanic Garden in town.
## From North Parish to town

Europeans first settled Boylston around 1706, in the northern part of today's town, most notably the Sawyer family, after the Nashaway sachems Sholan and George Tahanto deeded the land. Residents petitioned in 1697 to form a town, but the colonial governor denied the request. The town was a large part of Shrewsbury with the remainder from Lancaster, known as the North Parish of Shrewsbury from 1742 until it was incorporated as Boylston in 1786. A meeting house was built in 1743.

The name honors Ward Nicholas Boylston (1747 to 1828), a benefactor. The fund he set up in 1797 grew to $1,450 and paid for the town hall and school building. Residents once made a living from agriculture and from mills on the Nashua River, until construction of the Wachusett Reservoir ended that work.
## Housing that sits near the middle

The year in the middle of Boylston's housing is 1977, while the middle town lands on 1975. Units from 2000 or later make up 394 (20.8%), and 201 (10.6%) are from 2010 or later, which ranks 14th. Another 1,075 units (56.7%) predate 1980, close to the middle town's 57.2%. Detached houses are 1,588 units (83.8%), and 371 households rent (19.9%).

A worn oil boiler therefore usually triggers a comparison between a new oil unit, gas if a main can reach the house, and a heat pump.

Ask the department, and check masssave.com for the current terms.

faq.q: Are older Boylston houses harder to heat?
faq.a: Often, but not always. The median home dates from 1977, and 56.7% of units were built before 1980. Wall insulation and window quality differ between houses of that age, which is why we assess the home's heating load before quoting. The answer can differ a lot from the capacity of the unit being removed.

About one in five households rents: 371 of 1,864, or 19.9%, which ranks 20th of 50 and is above the 16.4% of the middle town. For a rental unit, the landlord normally pays for heat, and the heating system affects tenants and owners alike, so the equipment decision may involve more than one party.

body: ## Four other fuels in a town of oil

Oil leads by a wide margin, but the 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) shows four other fuels in use. Utility gas serves 315 homes (16.9%, 45th of 50). Electricity serves 203 (10.9%, 22nd). Bottled or tank gas serves 102 (5.5%, 17th), and wood serves 48 (2.6%).
A failed boiler or furnace can open any of those paths. An electric household can look at a heat pump, a gas household replaces like with like, and bottled gas, like oil, comes by delivery.
### Gas conversions and permits

Gas needs a main at or near the property, and that is the gas company's decision. If a switch is possible, a permit and a final inspection normally follow, and only licensed plumbers and gas fitters can pull the permit. The building department can describe the local process.
### Rental units

With 371 renter households (19.9%, 20th of 50), heating failures often involve a landlord. Rental boilers and furnaces tend to fail in cold snaps, and the state code treats heat as a landlord duty unless the lease says otherwise, with minimum temperatures that apply for the heating season (general information, not legal advice).
### Older houses

Boylston has 231 units from 1939 or earlier (12.2%) and 332 from 1940 to 1959 (17.5%). Together with the 512 units from 1960 to 1979, that is the pre-1980 group of 1,075 units. Houses that old differ in how much has been done to seal and insulate them, so the heating load assessment we do before quoting is what sets the new equipment size.
### If the heat goes out

Call (508) 786-8755 at any hour. Mass HVAC is licensed and insured, handles emergency calls around the clock, and provides a free written estimate before work starts. Our [maintenance page](/cities/boylston/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) covers keeping the new system healthy.

faq.q: Can a Boylston oil home switch to gas?
faq.a: Only if a gas main is on the street or can be extended, and the gas company decides that. Utility gas heats just 16.9% of homes, ranking 45th of 50, so most homes do not use it today. If gas is out of reach, that leaves oil, propane or a heat pump.

faq.q: Who pays for heat in a Boylston rental?
faq.a: The landlord, unless the lease says otherwise. The Massachusetts sanitary code sets minimum indoor temperatures for rentals through the heating season, lower overnight than during the day. That is general information, not legal advice, and a lease can change who pays.

faq.q: How do I know if my boiler needs replacing?
faq.a: Frequent repairs, a cracked heat exchanger, heavy soot or a unit near the end of its life all point toward replacement. A single failed part on a younger unit usually points toward repair. The written estimate should show both so you can compare before you decide.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Detached houses are 83.8% of Boylston's housing and the median owner-occupied home is worth $498,000. With 190 units in multi-unit buildings (10.0%), cooling jobs split between houses and attached or small multi-unit homes.
body: ## Houses, townhouses and small buildings

The 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) counts 1,588 detached houses among Boylston's 1,896 units, or 83.8%, ranking 15th of 50. Another 118 units are attached townhouses (6.2%), 76 are in two-unit buildings (4.0%), 65 are in buildings of three or four units (3.4%) and 49 are in buildings of five or more (2.6%). All multi-unit buildings together hold 190 units, or 10.0%, which ranks 40th.

That mix means two kinds of cooling job. A detached house can usually place equipment on any side. An attached or multi-unit home has shared walls, so the outdoor unit may need to sit on a ground pad or balcony, subject to the building's rules.
### Value and expectations
The median value of an owner-occupied Boylston home is $498,000, 36th of 50 and below the $579,150 of the middle town. Value alone says nothing about which system suits a house.
### Central or ductless

Central air needs ducts sized for cooling, and ducts built only for heating are often too small. Ductless mini-splits need no ducts and suit rooms that central air reaches poorly. A townhouse or small multi-unit home may favor one ductless head per zone, since it avoids work inside shared walls.
### Newer homes

Boylston has 394 units from 2000 or later (20.8%) and 201 from 2010 or later (10.6%), 14th of 50. Newer houses tend to be tighter, so a modest system may do the job, but oversizing is still a risk. A unit that is too big shuts off before it removes moisture and can leave the house feeling damp.
### Repairs and estimates

A failed capacitor or dirty coil is generally a repair. A failed compressor on old equipment usually leads to replacement. A free written estimate arrives before work starts. For equipment that cools and heats, see the [heat pump page](/cities/boylston/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Can I cool a Boylston townhouse or condo with ductless?
faq.a: Often, yes. Ductless mini-splits avoid ductwork, which helps where walls are shared. The outdoor unit still needs a permitted location, and an association or landlord may have rules. Boylston has 118 attached townhouse units, so it is worth asking about placement early.

faq.q: Is central air or ductless better for a detached house?
faq.a: It depends on ductwork. If the ducts are in good condition and sized for cooling, central air is a natural fit. If they are not, or if only a few rooms need cooling, ductless heads can be simpler. Many houses use both, with central air for the main floors and a head for an extra room.

faq.q: Why does an oversized air conditioner feel clammy?
faq.a: Because it cools the air quickly and shuts off before removing enough moisture. The air feels cool but damp. A unit sized to the house's load runs longer and steadier, which dries the air better. That is why sizing should begin with the building and its load.

body: ## The municipal utility is the starting point

Boylston's electric utility is the Boylston Municipal Light Department. Where a municipal utility serves the home, Mass Save heat pump rebates generally apply only to homes heated with natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor, and otherwise the municipal utility's own program applies. We do not state what that program pays, so ask the light department.
### What the heating mix implies

Utility gas heats 315 Boylston homes (16.9%), while oil heats 1,196 (64.2%), bottled gas 102 (5.5%) and electricity 203 (10.9%). An oil home is generally not a gas home, so for most of the town the municipal program is the one to ask about. A gas home may qualify under Mass Save, subject to that program's terms and to confirmation at masssave.com. The details of the statewide program are on our [heat pump page for the whole service area](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Weatherization and the age of the housing

Where Mass Save applies, the home must be sufficiently weatherized first. A house built in 2000 or later passes, and Boylston has 394 such units (20.8%). The 201 units from 2010 or later add to that. For the 1,075 units built before 1980 (56.7%), the route is an assessment.
### Oil to heat pump
With oil in 1,196 homes, the fuel-switch question is common. A heat pump replaces some or all of a delivered fuel with electricity, and cools in summer.
### Partial setups

A heat pump can carry most of the year while a working oil boiler takes the coldest days. That suits owners who prefer to keep their existing equipment. The sizing of both systems matters, and we assess the home's heating load first.
### Townhouses and small buildings

Boylston has 118 townhouse units and 190 units in multi-unit buildings. A ductless system can serve one unit without work inside shared walls, although outdoor placement may need approval from whoever manages the property.
See also our [cooling page](/cities/boylston/air-conditioning-installation-repair).

faq.q: Do Mass Save rebates apply in Boylston?
faq.a: Possibly, but not by default. Boylston is served by a municipal light department, and in those towns Mass Save heat pump rebates generally apply only to homes heated with natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor. Homes on oil or propane usually look to the municipal program instead. Terms can change, so confirm both.

faq.q: Is my 1977 house weatherized enough for a rebate?
faq.a: Not automatically. The median Boylston home dates from 1977, before the 2000 cutoff, so an assessment is the usual path. If it recommends under $1,000 of work, or past recommendations from 2013 or later were done, the home can pass. Ask whichever program applies to you.

faq.q: Should I keep my oil boiler and add a heat pump?
faq.a: It is a reasonable option. A partial setup lets the heat pump handle mild weather while the boiler covers the coldest days. With oil in 64.2% of Boylston homes, many houses start from that position. A heating load assessment sets the size of the heat pump, and the utility sets the rebate.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Oil heats 1,196 Boylston homes (64.2%), so the yearly burner cleaning is the main upkeep task for most systems. With 19.9% of households renting, tune-ups also depend on whether an owner or landlord books them.
body: ## An oil town's calendar
Oil heats about two thirds of Boylston's occupied homes. Each oil burner needs a cleaning once a year, ahead of the heating season. Leaving it undone is a common route to a no-heat call in January.
### Owners and tenants

The 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) counts 1,493 owner-occupied households (80.1%) and 371 renter households (19.9%, 20th of 50). In an owner-occupied house, the owner books service. In a rental, the landlord usually pays for heat, so a pre-season check is one way to avoid a failure in a cold snap, when rental boilers and furnaces tend to fail.
### Other fuels and systems

Gas serves 315 homes, electricity 203, bottled gas 102 and wood 48. A gas appliance is worth a yearly look at its burner, flue and controls. Bottled gas systems share that need. Electric heat pumps have no flame but do have filters, coils and drains to keep clear. A dirty filter or a blocked drain is easy to spot, and fixing it early prevents bigger faults.
### Age and wear

Boylston has 512 units from 1960 to 1979 (27.0%) and 427 from 1980 to 1999 (22.5%). Equipment from those decades, if still original, would be well into its working life. A planned visit can catch a worn part before it fails, such as an igniter, a nozzle, a motor or a belt. Parts like those cost little to replace on a schedule and much more when they fail at night.
### Few empty houses
Only 32 of Boylston's 1,896 units are vacant (1.7%), ranking 42nd. Anyone leaving a house empty for a long winter trip should still set a safe minimum temperature.
### A simple year
- **Late summer to early fall:** heating tune-up.
- **Spring:** cooling check on central air or ductless heads.
- **Anytime:** short cycling, odd smells or climbing bills are a reason to call early.
If a check shows the unit is beyond saving, our [heating page](/cities/boylston/heating-installation-repair) explains the next step.

faq.q: What does a yearly oil burner service include?
faq.a: Soot comes out, the filter and nozzle are replaced, and combustion is tested. Without that visit, deposits can build until efficiency drops or the burner quits during the worst of winter. Oil heats 64.2% of Boylston homes, so this is the task that applies to the largest group.

faq.q: Does a heat pump need tune-ups?
faq.a: Yes, though different ones. Filters, coils and condensate drains need attention, and refrigerant and electrical connections can be checked. Because a heat pump works in both seasons, it is used more hours a year than a stand-alone air conditioner, and a check can be timed for spring or fall.

faq.q: Who should book a tune-up for a rental unit?
faq.a: Usually the landlord, who normally pays for heat unless the lease says otherwise. A tenant can report symptoms such as short cycling or no heat. Boylston has 371 renter households, and a pre-season check can reduce cold-snap failures.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Boylston's housing runs from 231 units built in 1939 or earlier to 394 from 2000 or later, so air quality problems vary by house. Older homes can leak, newer ones can hold moisture, and a measurement should guide the fix.
body: ## One town, five generations of houses

The 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) divides Boylston's 1,896 housing units into bands: 231 from 1939 or earlier (12.2%), 332 from 1940 to 1959 (17.5%), 512 from 1960 to 1979 (27.0%), 427 from 1980 to 1999 (22.5%) and 394 from 2000 or later (20.8%). Air quality issues often follow the building era.
### Older houses

Houses from before 1960 often leak air through gaps. That dilutes some pollutants, but it also admits dust, pollen and damp basement air. Only 12.2% of Boylston units date from 1939 or earlier, below the 16.6% of the middle town, so the very oldest construction is a smaller share than usual. Before any renovation in an older house, a specialist should be asked about testing for hazardous legacy materials.
### Newer houses

Houses from 2000 or later are usually tighter. Boylston has 201 units built since 2010 (10.6%), ranking 14th of 50, a share that is above the 8.4% of the middle town. Inside a tight house, damp air, kitchen fumes and off-gassing from furniture linger when ventilation is weak. The usual remedy is a ventilator that swaps stale air for fresh.
### Combustion and oil

Oil heats 1,196 homes and wood heats 48. Flame appliances should be vented correctly and kept in tune, since combustion byproducts are both a safety and an air issue. Carbon monoxide detectors belong in any home that burns fuel.
### Humidity

Winter heat tends to dry the air, and summer brings the damp back. A hygrometer costs little and shows which problem you have. A humidifier, dehumidifier or ventilator then answers a measured need, not a guess.
### Ducts, filters and testing

Filters catch what passes through, so a clean one helps. Ducts deserve cleaning when you can see dirt or mold in them, or after pest or renovation damage. Air testing is a snapshot, so fixing the source, such as a damp basement or a leaking duct, is what keeps results from reverting. Equipment care also matters; see the [maintenance page](/cities/boylston/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups).

faq.q: Do newer Boylston houses have better air?
faq.a: Not necessarily. They are tighter, which can trap moisture and fumes without ventilation. With 394 units from 2000 or later, ventilation and humidity control matter. Older houses leak more and can have different problems. A measurement tells you which situation you have.

Only with a reason, such as visible dirt, mold or damage. Otherwise sealing leaks, changing filters and controlling humidity usually do more for air quality. Inspecting the system first shows whether cleaning would help.

faq.q: How can I control humidity in winter and summer?
faq.a: Measure first with a hygrometer. In winter, heated air can be too dry, and a humidifier tied to the system may help. In summer, a dehumidifier or a properly sized air conditioner removes moisture. A tight house may need a ventilator so fresh air still enters.
